subject: Private deployment performance & ops handoff: next steps
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha@clearmap.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Miller <devon@clearmap.io>
Date: 2028-06-29T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment performance — follow-up and pre-POC asks

Thanks for the demo today Jordan — helpful walkthrough. A few follow-ups from our infra and product teams so we can scope the private deployment POC. Quick summary of asks we will validate on our side and where we need Redwood input: 

- Streaming start latency (first-byte) target: aim for <= 500ms under steady-state for a 6–8 token prompt.
- Per-token generation tail: we'd like p95 <= 120ms when concurrency is under 100 streams.
- Throughput target: sustain 100 concurrent streaming sessions, peak bursts to 200 for short windows.
- VPN/Peering concerns: Our infra team runs NAT gateways behind a transit gateway; they requested recommended MTU, any port ranges to keep open, and expected throughput per tunnel for a 100-stream target.
- Egress: we need guidance on whether outbound model-serving traffic must go through a proxy or can be routed directly to Redwood inference nodes in the private deployment (we're on AWS).

I've attached a sketch of our traceroute from a staging host (clearmap_traceroute-output.txt) and a short list of our current tunnel specs. Can you confirm Redwood's recommended SLOs for a private on-prem/VPC deployment and what evidence (i.e., tests/traces) you need from us ahead of the POC kickoff?

Would like to lock a 2-week POC starting the week of 2028-07-15 if we can clear these items.

Thanks — Asha
Asha Patel
Head of Platform, ClearMap

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@clearmap.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment performance — follow-up and pre-POC asks

Hi Asha — great to meet you and the team yesterday. Short answers first: yes, the targets you listed are achievable in our private/VPC offering with the right pathing and host sizing; we'll scope a validation plan.

What we'll provide from Redwood in advance of the POC:
- Recommended SLO matrix (p50/p95/p99) for streaming-first-byte and per-token for the model class you selected.
- An SLO verification checklist (network probes, traceroutes, small client load generator config).
- A minimal reference deployment config (MTU, ENI sizing, expected throughput per tunnel).
- A short test harness for your infra team to run a controlled concurrency sweep (we can run it together during the kickoff).

Action items for your side before the kickoff:
- Provide a representative client IP/subnet that will be used in the POC so we can whitelist and run probes.
- Share a short sample prompt (6–8 tokens) and a longer prompt (50–200 tokens) so our perf team can simulate the same shape.
- Confirm whether the POC environment will use AWS Transit Gateway + NAT or a direct peering/VPC peering model.

Ben and Karthik — can your teams take point on the SLO matrix + test harness? Hannah, please coordinate ops runbook and the playbook for fallback (e.g., what we do if we see packet loss > 1% during the POC).

I'll attach a filled SLO template in the next email.

Cheers,
Jordan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@clearmap.io>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment performance — SLO proposal and network check list

Asha — attaching our populated SLO template (redwood_slo_template.xlsx) and a short checklist your network team can run. Highlights / assumptions in the sheet:

- Baseline host: 8x A100-equivalent for the model variant you chose (we list alternatives for smaller SKUs).
- Expected steady-state p95 per-token: ~90–120ms (depends on token size and KV cache behavior).
- Streaming start (first-byte) p95 target: <= 400–500ms when client-to-edge hop RTT is <= 30ms; add ~150–200ms if cross-region.
- Concurrency plan: a single dedicated pool can sustain ~120 concurrent streaming sessions for medium-length responses; we recommend autoscale to handle spikes to 200.
- Throughput sizing: plan for ~350 Mbps egress headroom for 200 streams (audio/video not included).

Network checklist (summary):
1) Ensure MTU >= 1400.
2) Keep TCP keepalive and idle timers tuned (we recommend 60s).
3) Open outbound ports TCP 443, and allow UDP for traceroute if you plan ICMP/UDP probing.
4) If using Transit Gateway + NAT, confirm the NAT throughput per AZ; if NAT is a bottleneck, use VPC peering or Direct Connect for high-throughput tunnels.
5) Provide a NAT/Firewall rule snapshot and a sample of your egress bandwidth during peak for us to review.

What we need from you by 2028-07-10 to hit the 2028-07-15 kickoff:
- Representative subnet(s) to whitelist.
- Confirmation of the tunnel type (Transit NAT vs VPC peering/Direct Connect).
- Sample prompt payloads and a brief spike plan (how long you expect bursts).

If you prefer, we can set a 30-minute network ops call Wednesday 2028-07-11 to walk your networking team through the checklist.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Asha Patel <asha@clearmap.io>

Subject: Re: Private deployment performance — confirming pre-POC timeline and ops call

Thanks Jordan and Ben — this looks good and very actionable. We're lining up the infra folks and will provide the subnet info + prompt samples by EOD 2028-07-10. Devon confirmed Transit Gateway + NAT for the initial POC (we're evaluating Direct Connect in parallel).

We accept the 07/11 network ops call — can you do 2028-07-11 14:00 UTC? We'll invite our network lead and a security rep. Also please include the test harness link in the calendar invite so we can run through the steps in the session.

One question before the call: for the autoscale behavior you mentioned, do you have a recommended warm-up window to avoid cold-start latency impacting the POC baseline? If so, what's the suggested pre-warm concurrency and how long before the test?

Appreciate the rapid turn here — Asha
